events.text:
**Pick: Grand Haven, but only by a small margin. I'd rate every port about 1 (below average) for pier salmon this week.** The newest reports are from 2022-05-18, which is 6 days old.

| Port | Pier rating | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Haven | 1 (low end of 1–2) | Pier anglers caught "a few coho salmon on alewives or while casting orange spoons" (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18). |
| St. Joseph | 1 | "an occasional coho" on spawn (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18). |
| South Haven | 1 | "Pier fishing remained slow but there was an occasional coho caught on spawn" (South Haven, 2022-05-18). |
| Muskegon | 1 (a guess) | There was no pier report for Muskegon in the data. |

**How to fish Grand Haven:** Cast orange spoons or fish alewife. Those are the only pier lures the Grand Haven report names (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18). At the other piers, spawn was the bait that caught coho.

**What the reports say**
- Boat fishing is much better than pier fishing, and the fish are offshore.
  - Grand Haven boats had good action (quality 3), with fish 30–120 ft down in 130–240 ft of water (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18).
  - Muskegon boats were also good (quality 3), with fish 35–90 ft down in 120–200 ft of water on green and blue spoons and white flies (Muskegon, 2022-05-18).
  - St. Joseph boats had good coho fishing (quality 3), mostly on spoons (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18).
  - South Haven boats had fair fishing (quality 2), with fish spread out from 30 ft of water to deeper (South Haven, 2022-05-18).
- Pier results have been poor all spring at St. Joseph and South Haven. They were rated 0–1 on every report from 04-06 to 05-18. Grand Haven's pier was rated slow (0) on 04-27 (Grand Haven, 2022-04-27).
- Water temperature (measured by buoy) averaged 52 F off Grand Haven and Muskegon and 53 F off St. Joseph and South Haven this past week. That is within the 52–58 F range salmon prefer (NY DEC, general guidance). It had dropped 3–4 F over the week.
- The database has no earlier seasons for this date, so I have no history to compare against.

**My read**
- I'd expect the Grand Haven pier to be slightly ahead. Its report is the only one that mentions pier anglers using more than spawn, and alewives and spoons are what the reports show catching fish there.
- The 3–4 F drop this week could mean cold water is moving toward shore. That's a possible upwelling sign (Michigan Sea Grant, general guidance), but I can't confirm it. The same buoys showed a +5 to +6 F rise in the 05-18 reports, so the drop may just be a pullback from that warm-up.
- I'd expect the best pier bite to come on mornings after a north or east wind.
- Muskegon's 1 is purely inferred from its good boat fishing. Don't read it as a report of pier fishing there.

**Caveats**
- The wind forecast and the modeled cold-layer depth weren't available (the tool ran in backtest mode), so I can't say whether a wind shift is coming. Check the forecast before you go.
- The pier catches reported were singles ("a few," "occasional").

**Bulletins relied on**
- 2022-05-18 (all four ports): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3186585
- 2022-04-27: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3155afc
- 2022-04-20: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3145666
